findings.title: Validate imported answers against the built-in question catalog
findings.problem: trialEntries accepts arbitrary question IDs, categories, difficulties, sources and keys from localStorage. importTrialLive then treats those fields as authoritative inputs to XP and updateAbility, even creating new ability categories. Limiting the array to five rows does not make those rows valid trial answers. The tampered-storage test actually expects 150 XP from fabricated rows, including nonexistent built-in ID 0 and altered difficulties, so it passes while accepting the corruption its title claims to prevent.
findings.failure_scenario: A malformed trial contains a recent timestamp and an answer such as {id:999999, source:"bank", cat:"Unknown", diff:3, correct:true}. Signing into an empty account imports it, awards XP, creates an ability category, and changes subsequent readiness calculations despite that question never being available in the guest trial.
findings.fix: Resolve every imported ID against the actual guest-eligible built-in catalog. Reject unknown IDs and incompatible identities; obtain source, key, category, difficulty, population and stem from the catalog rather than the stored row. Change the tampered-storage test to verify that fabricated questions and altered metadata cannot affect XP, ability or the answer log.

findings.title: A timed-out request can still overwrite a newer progress snapshot
findings.problem: The timeout aborts the client request and releases the queue through Promise.race, but subsequent upserts contain no server-enforced revision or compare-and-set condition. Aborting a fetch is not proof that the server canceled an already accepted database operation. The queue therefore cannot guarantee its documented promise that an older request cannot land after the next save. The tests model abort as preventing the write itself, which does not exercise this failure.
findings.failure_scenario: Save A is accepted but delayed server-side. After eight seconds the client abandons A and starts save B containing additional answers. B completes and the UI reports success. If A subsequently commits, its older whole-blob upsert erases the additional answers. I could not verify a backend guarantee that disconnecting these Supabase requests cancels their transactions.
findings.fix: Enforce ordering at the persistence boundary with a server-managed revision and conditional update/RPC, rejecting stale snapshots and handling conflicts without dropping answers. Add a test where the server commits an abandoned request after a newer request; merely making the mock refuse writes after AbortSignal is insufficient.

findings.title: Keep overdue corrected questions visible when their catalog rows are missing
findings.problem: catalogMissCards discards every item whose latest answer is correct. Corrected questions still have active spaced-review schedules, and reviewPools normally serves them again when due. If their catalog rows are unavailable, this filter removes them without providing the recovery card used for other saved reviews.
findings.failure_scenario: A student misses bank:2500, answers it correctly on review, and receives a later review date. On that date the bank request fails and the app uses bundled questions. Because the latest answer is correct, no catalog-miss card is created; Today and Review Misses silently omit the overdue scheduled review.
findings.fix: Build unavailable-review cards from both current misses and due scheduled bank identities. Pass the schedule and local day into this recovery logic, and test a wrong-then-correct question whose next review is due while its catalog row is unavailable.

assessment: Changes are needed before release. The new save queue does not establish server-side write ordering, trial imports trust fields that can corrupt ability calculations, and catalog recovery omits some overdue reviews. This was a static review; I did not execute the tests.
